title: Tensor-Hom adjunction for modules over a ringed space
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space (a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings on its opens) and $\mathcal A,\mathcal G,\mathcal F$ $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ be the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with $t_W:\mathcal A(W)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(W)}\mathcal G(W)\to(\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)(W)$ the components of the sheafification map, and $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ the sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]; for $\eta\in\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_W}(\mathcal G|_W,\mathcal F|_W)$ write $\eta_{W'}:\mathcal G(W')\to\mathcal F(W')$ ($W'\subseteq W$ open) for its components. Then for every $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\tilde\varphi:\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ with $\tilde\varphi_W(t_W(a\otimes g))=(\varphi_W(a))_W(g)$ for all opens $W$, $a\in\mathcal A(W)$, $g\in\mathcal G(W)$, and $\varphi\mapsto\tilde\varphi$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A,\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ of $\mathcal O_X(X)$-modules, natural in $\mathcal A$ (for $\alpha:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$: $\widetilde{\varphi\circ\alpha}=\tilde\varphi\circ(\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G})$).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CN (label lemma-internal-hom, line 3534; tag verified in tags/tags line 1768), the 'in particular' clause; its proof ('the analogue of Algebra, Lemma 00DE (algebra-lemma-hom-from-tensor-product); the proof is the same, and is omitted'); cited as 'Modules, Lemma 01CN' in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YB

proof.text: (Conventions.) The opens of $X$ with open coverings form a site, $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on it, and its ring of global sections is $\mathcal O_X(X)$; so the definitions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pur-sheaf-hom], [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module], [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] apply. Write $\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G$ for the presheaf tensor product, $(\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G)(W)=\mathcal A(W)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(W)}\mathcal G(W)$, whose restriction along $W'\subseteq W$ sends $a\otimes g$ to $a|_{W'}\otimes g|_{W'}$, and $t:\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G\to\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ for the sheafification map, an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map of presheaves of modules with components $t_W$. For $\eta\in\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)(W)$ the components $\eta_{W'}$ ($W'\subseteq W$) are $\mathcal O_X(W')$-linear and commute with restriction ($\eta_{W''}(g|_{W''})=\eta_{W'}(g)|_{W''}$ for $W''\subseteq W'$); the restriction of $\eta$ to $W_1\subseteq W$ has components $(\eta|_{W_1})_{W'}=\eta_{W'}$ ($W'\subseteq W_1$); and $f\in\mathcal O_X(W)$ acts by $(f\eta)_{W'}=f|_{W'}\,\eta_{W'}$, sums being taken componentwise. For $s\in\mathcal O_X(X)$ and a morphism $\chi$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, $(s\chi)_W=s|_W\,\chi_W$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CN (lemma-internal-hom, line 3534), 'in particular' clause; proof: 'the analogue of Algebra, Lemma 00DE (algebra.tex line 1906)', written out on sections

proof.text: (From $\varphi$ to a map of presheaves, on each open: Algebra 00DE.) Let $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ be $\mathcal O_X$-linear and $W$ open. The map $c_W:\mathcal A(W)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X(W)}(\mathcal G(W),\mathcal F(W))$, $a\mapsto(\varphi_W(a))_W$, is well defined since each $(\varphi_W(a))_W$ is $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear, and is $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear: $\varphi_W$ is $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear, and by step 1 $(f\eta+\eta')_W=f\,\eta_W+\eta'_W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying] (with $R=\mathcal O_X(W)$, $M=\mathcal A(W)$, $N=\mathcal G(W)$, $P=\mathcal F(W)$) there is a unique $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear $\psi_W:\mathcal A(W)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(W)}\mathcal G(W)\to\mathcal F(W)$ with $\psi_W(a\otimes g)=(\varphi_W(a))_W(g)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DE (lemma-hom-from-tensor-product, line 1906) and its proof, applied on the sections over $W$ (Modules 01CN, proof)

proof.text: ($\psi=(\psi_W)_W$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$.) Each $\psi_W$ is $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear by step 2. For $W'\subseteq W$, $a\in\mathcal A(W)$, $g\in\mathcal G(W)$: $\psi_{W'}(a|_{W'}\otimes g|_{W'})=(\varphi_{W'}(a|_{W'}))_{W'}(g|_{W'})=((\varphi_W(a))|_{W'})_{W'}(g|_{W'})=(\varphi_W(a))_{W'}(g|_{W'})=((\varphi_W(a))_W(g))|_{W'}=\psi_W(a\otimes g)|_{W'}$, using in turn that $\varphi$ commutes with restriction, the formula $(\eta|_{W'})_{W'}=\eta_{W'}$ and the naturality of $\eta=\varphi_W(a)$ (step 1). So the two maps $\mathcal A(W)\otimes\mathcal G(W)\to\mathcal F(W')$, $x\mapsto\psi_{W'}(x|_{W'})$ and $x\mapsto\psi_W(x)|_{W'}$, both additive and $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear for the $\mathcal O_X(W)$-module structure on $\mathcal F(W')$ through $\mathcal O_X(W)\to\mathcal O_X(W')$, agree on all $a\otimes g$, hence are equal by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying]. Thus $\psi$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DE (lemma-hom-from-tensor-product, line 1906) and its proof, applied on the sections over $W$ (Modules 01CN, proof)

proof.text: (From a map of presheaves back to $\varphi$.) Let $\psi:\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ be a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. For $W$ open and $a\in\mathcal A(W)$ define $\varphi_W(a)$ by $(\varphi_W(a))_{W'}(g)=\psi_{W'}(a|_{W'}\otimes g)$ for $W'\subseteq W$, $g\in\mathcal G(W')$. Each component is $\mathcal O_X(W')$-linear in $g$ ($\psi_{W'}$ is linear and $\otimes$ is linear in the second factor); for $W''\subseteq W'$, $\psi_{W''}(a|_{W''}\otimes g|_{W''})=\psi_{W'}(a|_{W'}\otimes g)|_{W''}$ by the naturality of $\psi$ and the restriction rule of $\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G$; so $\varphi_W(a)\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_W}(\mathcal G|_W,\mathcal F|_W)=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)(W)$. The map $\varphi_W$ is $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear: $(\varphi_W(fa+a'))_{W'}(g)=\psi_{W'}(f|_{W'}a|_{W'}\otimes g+a'|_{W'}\otimes g)=f|_{W'}(\varphi_W(a))_{W'}(g)+(\varphi_W(a'))_{W'}(g)=(f\varphi_W(a)+\varphi_W(a'))_{W'}(g)$ by step 1. It commutes with restriction to $W_1\subseteq W$: $(\varphi_{W_1}(a|_{W_1}))_{W'}(g)=\psi_{W'}(a|_{W'}\otimes g)=(\varphi_W(a))_{W'}(g)=((\varphi_W(a))|_{W_1})_{W'}(g)$ for $W'\subseteq W_1$. So $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DE (lemma-hom-from-tensor-product, line 1906) and its proof, applied on the sections over $W$ (Modules 01CN, proof)

proof.text: (Steps 2–3 and step 4 are mutually inverse.) Starting from $\varphi$, let $\psi$ be as in steps 2–3 and $\varphi'$ as in step 4: $(\varphi'_W(a))_{W'}(g)=\psi_{W'}(a|_{W'}\otimes g)=(\varphi_{W'}(a|_{W'}))_{W'}(g)=(\varphi_W(a))_{W'}(g)$ by the computation of step 3, so $\varphi'=\varphi$. Starting from $\psi$, let $\varphi$ be as in step 4 and $\psi'$ as in steps 2–3: $\psi'_W(a\otimes g)=(\varphi_W(a))_W(g)=\psi_W(a|_W\otimes g)=\psi_W(a\otimes g)$, so $\psi'_W=\psi_W$ by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying]. Hence $\varphi\mapsto\psi$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A,\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F))$ onto the set of morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$, and $\psi$ is the unique such morphism with $\psi_W(a\otimes g)=(\varphi_W(a))_W(g)$ for all $W,a,g$ (uniqueness again by [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying] on each $W$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DE (lemma-hom-from-tensor-product, line 1906) and its proof, applied on the sections over $W$ (Modules 01CN, proof)

proof.text: (Sheafification.) $\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ is the sheafification of $\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G$ with map $t$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; by the universal property of sheafification of presheaves of modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\chi\mapsto\chi\circ t$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ onto the morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal A\otimes_p\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$. Given $\varphi$, let $\tilde\varphi$ be the unique morphism with $\tilde\varphi\circ t=\psi$ ($\psi$ from step 2); then $\tilde\varphi_W(t_W(a\otimes g))=\psi_W(a\otimes g)=(\varphi_W(a))_W(g)$. If $\chi$ is any $\mathcal O_X$-linear map with $\chi_W(t_W(a\otimes g))=(\varphi_W(a))_W(g)$ for all $W,a,g$, then $\chi\circ t$ is a morphism of presheaves of modules with the formula of step 5, so $\chi\circ t=\psi$ by the uniqueness in step 5, and $\chi=\tilde\varphi$ by the uniqueness in the universal property. The map $\varphi\mapsto\tilde\varphi$ is the composite of the bijection of step 5 and the inverse of $\chi\mapsto\chi\circ t$, hence a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A,\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Modules, Section 01CA (section-tensor-product: $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ is the sheafification of the presheaf tensor product) with the universal property of sheafification of presheaves of modules; Modules 01CN, proof

proof.text: ($\mathcal O_X(X)$-linearity.) Let $s\in\mathcal O_X(X)$ and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ as above. The $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\chi=s\tilde\varphi_1+\tilde\varphi_2$ [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module] satisfies $\chi_W(t_W(a\otimes g))=s|_W(\varphi_{1,W}(a))_W(g)+(\varphi_{2,W}(a))_W(g)=(s|_W\varphi_{1,W}(a)+\varphi_{2,W}(a))_W(g)=((s\varphi_1+\varphi_2)_W(a))_W(g)$, by the formula of step 6, the action $(f\eta)_W=f\,\eta_W$ of step 1, and $(s\varphi_1)_W(a)=s|_W\varphi_{1,W}(a)$ [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module]. By the uniqueness in step 6, $\chi=\widetilde{s\varphi_1+\varphi_2}$; so $\varphi\mapsto\tilde\varphi$ is $\mathcal O_X(X)$-linear, hence an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X(X)$-modules.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CN (lemma-internal-hom, line 3534), 'in particular' clause; proof: 'the analogue of Algebra, Lemma 00DE (algebra.tex line 1906)', written out on sections

proof.text: (Naturality in $\mathcal A$.) Let $\alpha:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ be $\mathcal O_X$-linear, with $t':\mathcal A'\otimes_p\mathcal G\to\mathcal A'\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ the sheafification map. The maps $\alpha_W\otimes\mathrm{id}:\mathcal A'(W)\otimes\mathcal G(W)\to\mathcal A(W)\otimes\mathcal G(W)$ (defined by [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying]) form a morphism of presheaves of modules $\alpha\otimes_p\mathrm{id}$ (checked on pure tensors as in step 3), and $\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}$ is the morphism of sheafifications it induces, i.e. the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map with $(\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G})\circ t'=t\circ(\alpha\otimes_p\mathrm{id})$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Then $(\tilde\varphi\circ(\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}))_W(t'_W(a'\otimes g))=\tilde\varphi_W(t_W(\alpha_W(a')\otimes g))=(\varphi_W(\alpha_W(a')))_W(g)=((\varphi\circ\alpha)_W(a'))_W(g)$ by step 6, so by the uniqueness in step 6 (applied to $\mathcal A'$ and $\varphi\circ\alpha$), $\widetilde{\varphi\circ\alpha}=\tilde\varphi\circ(\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G})$.
